{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by time-to-target, success rate, path efficiency, average speed, and angular dispersion?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation yielded the highest mean success rate (0.780) and the fastest mean time-to-target (2.56 s), with the highest mean average speed (12.83 units/s) and highest mean angular dispersion (0.399).",
    "Bright Visual Only performed similarly to Combined on success rate (0.785) but with slightly slower time-to-target (2.61 s) and lower angular dispersion (0.387).",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only showed intermediate performance: success rates of 0.673 and 0.685 respectively, time-to-target around 3.0-3.1 s, and lower path efficiency (~0.43-0.44) compared to Combined and Bright Visual Only (~0.50).",
    "Sham stimulation produced markedly inferior performance across all metrics: lowest success rate (0.273), slowest time-to-target (4.68 s), lowest path efficiency (0.308), slowest average speed (10.74 units/s), and lowest angular dispersion (0.236).",
    "Sample size varied substantially across paradigms: Combined dominated with 48,846 trials (63.7% of data), while Sham had only 3,505 trials (4.6%).",
    "Path efficiency and angular dispersion showed notable variability within paradigms (e.g., Combined path efficiency SD implies high variation, and sample rows show values ranging from 0.07 to 1.18).",
    "Across all 8 mice, Sham consistently produced the worst performance and Combined the best or near-best performance, though some individual variation existed (e.g., SC11LM showed particularly poor Sham performance with 0.067 success rate)."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sham versus all active stimulation paradigms showed the largest absolute differences: success rate gap of ~0.41-0.51, time-to-target difference of ~1.7-2.1 s, and path efficiency difference of ~0.12-0.20.",
    "Combined and Bright Visual Only versus Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only showed clear separation in success rates (~0.78 vs ~0.68) and path efficiency (~0.50 vs ~0.43).",
    "Angular dispersion was highest in Combined (0.399) and lowest in Sham (0.236), with a monotonic ordering suggesting more variable heading directions with multimodal stimulation.",
    "Average speed showed a narrower range (10.74-12.83 units/s) but still distinguished Sham from active conditions (~1.1-2.1 units/s slower)."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The data strongly suggest that any form of sensory or motor stimulation substantially improves navigation performance compared to no stimulation. Combined multimodal stimulation (ICMS + visual) and bright visual stimulation alone appear most effective, producing faster, more successful, and more efficient trajectories. Dim visual stimulation and ICMS alone provide intermediate benefit. The low angular dispersion in Sham trials indicates more directed, less exploratory heading behavior, possibly reflecting disorientation or lack of sensory feedback to guide navigation. These findings support the use of combined sensory-motor stimulation paradigms for restoring or augmenting navigation function in mouse models.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes across paradigms (Combined: 48,846 trials vs Sham: 3,505 trials) reduces precision for Sham estimates and may introduce bias if trial allocation was not randomized.",
    "No statistical tests (e.g., ANOVA, mixed-effects models) were performed; all comparisons are descriptive and effect sizes are uncertain without confidence intervals or p-values.",
    "Mouse-level variation is substantial and unaccounted for in aggregate means—some mice showed different rank-orderings of paradigm effectiveness (e.g., SC11L1RF had higher success with ICMS Only than Combined).",
    "Path efficiency distributions appear right-skewed (max 29.8 from overview vs means ~0.43-0.50), suggesting potential outliers or non-standard calculation that may affect interpretation.",
    "Temperature was fixed at 1.0 for LLM generation, but this is a data analysis parameter, not an experimental manipulation; the causal structure of the original experiment (stimulation delivery) is unclear from these artifacts.",
    "No information on trial structure, training history, or whether mice were naive to paradigms is provided."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model with Mouse as random intercept, Stim Paradigm as fixed effect, and each response variable as outcome, using appropriate distributions (e.g., binomial for Success, log-normal or robust regression for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency given right skew). Include planned contrasts comparing Combined vs Sham, Combined vs single-modality conditions, and Bright vs Dim Visual to quantify effect sizes with confidence intervals. Examine Mouse × Paradigm interactions to identify individual differences in stimulation responsiveness. Finally, assess whether angular dispersion mediates the relationship between stimulation and path efficiency using causal mediation analysis."
}
